headline: Wet, breezy week ahead, with a stronger storm midweek and coastal flooding risk.
summary: A cold pocket of air sitting offshore keeps scattered showers over western Washington today, with highs in the 40s inland. Pacific storms then take over, bringing steadier rain Monday and a stronger system Tuesday into Wednesday as a low pressure center deepens near the coast. Another system follows Thursday, so the wet pattern lasts all week. Mountain snow follows in the Olympics and Cascades, and gusty winds and high surf are expected along the coast. The main worry is coastal flooding, especially on Grays Harbor during Wednesday's high tides, and the Skokomish River may approach flood stage. Forecasters are fairly confident in a wet week but less sure of exact timing, strength, and tide impacts.
